conditions
conditions · 5 records
  1. Purchase commitment schedule excludes cancelable-without-penalty agreements and unconditional purchase commitments with one year or less remaining; this is not a complete next-year procurement total.
  2. 5-year customer lease backstop: on default, covered difference between85% of outstanding lease obligations and disposal proceeds; remedies include assuming lease, selling rights at fixed price under conditions, or sale of racks. Fair value described as immaterial; none paid. Gross29bn is neither recognized debt nor loss estimate.
  3. Conditional42bn notes would be issued BY customer TO Broadcom, only for customer lease obligations, if conditions met; none issued as ofAug2. This is potential funding/credit exposure, not Broadcom convertible debt or guaranteed revenue.
  4. Unvested RSUs, future SBC expense and current diluted weighted shares are different quantities. Unrecognized18.221bn is not award market value.
  5. Operating/finance leases need full reconciliation before final equity bridge; annual combined debt/lease tag and current debt tags differ.

invalidators
invalidators · 6 records
  1. AI customer concentration and development milestones; customers may insource architectures or reduce spend.
  2. Land/power/shell readiness can block shipment even when silicon supply is secured.
  3. HBM cost pass-through inflates revenue while compressing percentage gross margin; revenue multiples mislead.
  4. XPV credit backstop, conditional notes and supplier commitments correlate with AI downturn; physical capex understates economic capital.
  5. VMware renewal, pricing, customer migration and competition; software cannot be assumed to offset every semiconductor downturn.
  6. Long-lived acquisition intangibles, tax benefits, amortization and SBC distort simple GAAP/non-GAAP comparisons.

reported Fact
Majority of new software contracts no longer have termination-for-convenience provisions; additional license revenue recognized on contracts without termination rights contributed to Q3 software growth.
analytical Implication
Do not read29% quarterly software growth as wholly recurring organic demand. Model license timing, renewal economics and cash conversion separately.

ticker

methodology
Original prior-quarter issuer guidance matched to first reported same-period actual. Revenue is an approximate point estimate, not a range: beats are signed errors, not range-coverage misses. Missing comparable metrics are null, never zero. Annual targets and multi-year AI targets are separate from quarterly corporate revenue.

rationale
rationale · 8 fields
growth
75/65/30% early rates replace an undifferentiated35% input. Current Q4 corporate34.8bn and AI21.7bn guidance, then management FY27AI115bn/FY28AI230bn, justify a steeper near-term trajectory but not indefinite doubling. An illustrative50bn non-AI/software layer gives fiscal corporate165bn/280bn; proposed rollingY1/Y2 155.932bn/257.288bn remain below those cross-checks. The50bn layer is analyst judgment, not management consolidated guidance.
horizon
Three early years capture custom-accelerator ramps with current customers; total10-year maturation recognizes concentration, competitive insourcing and architecture risk. Bull15-year scenario tests durable platform extension;20years unjustified by current evidence.
margin
Model GAAP EBIT after SBC and amortization;53/55/54% early then45%. Current nonGAAP67.91% excludes material SBC/amortization; pass-through memory costs lower percentage gross margin even as dollars grow. Gradual amortization runoff may support GAAP margin, but ongoing M&A/replacement IP costs cannot be assumed away.
capital
2x forward incremental sales/net reinvestment is judgment, not historical book ratio. Require explicit capex/working-capital/credit-support overlays, especially Q4capex1.4bn outlook and new production facilities. Gross debt-funded acquisition capital and goodwill distort historic bookROIC.
tax
20% normalized, above near-term~16% nonGAAP tax outlook; FY25 negative GAAP effective tax is discrete and unsustainable.
WACC
11% nominalUSD base versus prior10%; reflects commonOct16 risk-free5.09%,4.5% chosen ERP and unmeasured high concentration/credit cyclicality. Rounded risk judgment, not a regression-estimated WACC. Test10–13%.
terminal
2.5% growth,20% ROIC, requiring12.5% terminalNOPAT reinvestment. Sustained returns are analyst assumptions; no CEO premium.
claims
Keep full bridge gated for leases, equity awards and conditional financing. The29bn backstop and42bn customer-note capacity require state-contingent expected loss/capital modeling, not full automatic subtraction or zero.
price Calibration
false
implementation Caveat
Negative revenue growth must not mechanically create capital-release cash while capacity obligations/capex remain. Use maintenance/capacity minimums and correlated counterparty downside before an investable valuation.

bounded Model Gaps
bounded Model Gaps · 5 records
  1. Valuation-date stub and post-anchor cash/claims/share roll-forward not integrated; this is a forecast-origin operating EV, not October 17 equity value.
  2. No probability weighting or share-price calibration. Source forecast assumptions are judgments, not reported facts.
  3. Enterprise-to-equity bridge is not computed here; consult the company-specific claim register for resolved evidence, assumptions and remaining uncertainties. Zero is not evidence of absence.
  4. Selected S:C 2 and tax 20% retained. Capital rule is provisional; verified gross capex, depreciation, WC, commitment and funding schedules are unavailable.
  5. Final explicit S:C remains 2. Terminal ROIC policy changes investment intensity; disclosed FCFF transition is not silently smoothed.
